drug_class: Angiotensin II Receptor Blocker (ARB) combined with a Thiazide Diuretic
purpose: This combination medication is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). By lowering your blood pressure, it helps reduce your risk of having a heart attack or stroke. It combines two medicines into one convenient pill to make it easier to manage your blood pressure.
how_it_works: Valsartan works by blocking a chemical in your body called angiotensin II, which normally causes your blood vessels to tighten and squeeze. By blocking it, your blood vessels relax and open up, making it easier for your heart to pump blood. Hydrochlorothiazide is a water pill that helps your kidneys remove extra salt and water from your body, which also helps lower your blood pressure.
common_side_effects: Dizziness, especially when standing up quickly. Feeling tired or lightheaded. Increased urination from the water pill. Headache. Low potassium levels, which may cause muscle cramps or weakness. Dry cough is less common with this medicine than some other blood pressure drugs.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm your unborn baby. Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes unless your doctor says it is okay. Be careful in hot weather or during exercise, as you may get dehydrated more easily. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, diabetes, or gout. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is one tablet once a day, typically containing 80mg or 160mg of valsartan combined with 12.5mg of hydrochlorothiazide. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how well your blood pressure is controlled, up to a maximum of 320mg valsartan with 25mg hydrochlorothiazide once daily. Take it at the same time each day, with or without food.
